title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E593 builds continued fractions from series. Theorem IX (previous page) states the following. If s = ax/(αy) − abx²/(αβy²) + abcx³/(αβγy³) − …, then ax/s = αy + αbxy/(βy − bx + βcxy/(γy − cx + …)). This is an equivalence transformation: the convergents of the continued fraction are exactly the partial sums of the series.

In §§52–55 Euler takes Z = ∫₀^z t^{m−1}(1+tⁿ)^{k/n−1} dt. He writes Z = v(1+zⁿ)^{k/n} and obtains the linear ODE (1+zⁿ)v′ + k zⁿ⁻¹ v = z^{m−1}. Solving it by undetermined coefficients gives v = z^m/m − (m+k)/(m(m+n)) z^{m+n} + …. In modern terms v = (z^m/m)·₂F₁(1, (m+k)/n; (m+n)/n; −zⁿ). This is Euler's (Pfaff's) transformation applied to Z = (z^m/m)·₂F₁(1−k/n, m/n; m/n+1; −zⁿ).

On this page:
- §55 factors out z^{m−n}/m.
- §56 defines V = mZ/(z^{m−n}(1+zⁿ)^{k/n}), so that V = zⁿ − (m+k)/(m+n) z²ⁿ + …. It then puts zⁿ = x/y to match Theorem IX, with a = 1, b = m+k, c = m+n+k, … and α = 1, β = m+n, γ = m+2n, ….
- §57 gives x/V = y + (m+k)xy/((m+n)y − (m+k)x + (m+n)(m+n+k)xy/((m+2n)y − (m+n+k)x + …)). Its value is x z^{m−n}(1+zⁿ)^{k/n}/(mZ).
- §58 takes m = 1, n = 2, k = 1, so Z = arsinh z. Then V = z·arsinh z/√(1+z²) = z² − (2/3)z⁴ + (2·4)/(3·5) z⁶ − …. With z² = x/y this gives √(x(x+y))/ln((√x + √(x+y))/√y) = y + 1·2xy/(3y − 2x + 3·4xy/(5y − 4x + 5·6xy/(7y − 6x + …))).
- The next page specializes to (x, y) = (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3). The last gives a continued fraction for 4/ln 3.

The purpose is to illustrate the new series-to-continued-fraction method on a family of integrals: binomial/hypergeometric integrals, here arsinh.
errors: No mathematical errors. Coefficients, the matching with Theorem IX, the substitution z² = x/y and the closed form √(x/(x+y))·ln((√x + √(x+y))/√y) all check out.
Minor wording slip in §56: Euler writes 'valores ipsius v' where V is meant.

At x = y (z = 1, the next page) the underlying alternating series is only conditionally and slowly convergent. Because the continued fraction's convergents equal the partial sums, the continued fraction gives no acceleration; Euler does not remark on this.

ideas.what: Conversion of a series into an equivalent continued fraction whose convergents are the partial sums (Theorem IX applied).
ideas.modern_name: Euler's continued fraction formula (series ↔ continued fraction equivalence)
ideas.where_published: E593 itself; related in E247 (De fractionibus continuis observationes) and Introductio in analysin infinitorum ch. 18

ideas.what: Writing the integral of z^{m−1}(1+zⁿ)^{k/n−1} as (1+zⁿ)^{k/n} times a power series, found from a first-order linear ODE by undetermined coefficients.
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Pfaff transformation giving ₂F₁(1, b; c; −zⁿ) for incomplete beta-type integrals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; Pfaff (1797) for the general transformation
ideas.where_published: Institutiones calculi integralis vol. I and numerous Euler papers on such series

ideas.what: Series for arsinh z/√(1+z²) with coefficients (2·4···2j)/(3·5···(2j+1)), and the resulting continued fraction for √(x(x+y))/ln((√x + √(x+y))/√y).
ideas.modern_name: Series for arcsinh(z)/√(1+z²) (Euler series for arcsin/√(1−z²) with z → iz)
ideas.where_published: Euler's work on arcsin series, e.g. Institutiones calculi differentialis / E-papers on arcsin

deep.surprise_reason: A routine worked application of Euler's well-known series-to-continued-fraction equivalence to a hypergeometric/arsinh series. The results are correct and standard; nothing unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: §57 denominator tail: the image appears to read '(m+3n)y−(m+2n+k)x − etc.'; the sign is immaterial (it should continue with '+ (m+3n)(m+3n+k)xy/…').
§56: 'istos valores ipsius v' is as printed, though V is intended.
